outputs.L1: Disclosed are a solar cell module and a method for manufacturing the same. The solar cell module includes a plurality of cell cutting pieces stacked and connected in series, and a connector configured to connect two adjacent cell cutting pieces in series. The plurality of cell cutting pieces are cut from a solar cell, and each cell cutting piece includes a front electrode and a back electrode. The connector includes a first surface configured to connect to the front electrode and a second surface configured to connect to the back electrode. The first surface is provided with alternating first connecting areas and first disconnecting areas, and the second surface is provided with alternating second connecting areas and second disconnecting areas. Projections of the first disconnecting areas on the first surface overlap with projections of the second connecting areas on the first surface. The front electrode is configured to connect to the first connecting areas, and the back electrode is configured to connect to the second connecting areas. The solar cell module provides improved flexibility, thereby reducing the likelihood of breakage of grid lines and cells.
outputs.L2: Disclosed are a solar cell module and a process for producing it. The module comprises multiple cut cell sections that are stacked and electrically coupled in series. These cut sections are obtained by dividing a solar cell, and each section has a front electrode and a rear electrode. A connector is configured to place two neighboring cut cell sections in series connection. The connector has a first face for coupling to the front electrode and a second face for coupling to the rear electrode. On the first face, first connection regions and first non-connection regions are arranged alternately, while on the second face, second connection regions and second non-connection regions are also arranged alternately. When the first non-connection regions are projected onto the first face, those projections coincide with the projections of the second connection regions on the first face. The front electrode is configured to attach to the first connection regions, and the rear electrode is configured to attach to the second connection regions. This solar cell module offers enhanced flexibility, making grid lines and cells less prone to fracture.

A solar cell module and a method for manufacturing the same are disclosed. The solar cell module is designed to provide improved flexibility and durability while maintaining reliable electrical connection between solar cell portions.

The solar cell module includes a plurality of cell cutting pieces formed by cutting a solar cell into multiple sections. These cell cutting pieces are stacked or arranged in sequence and electrically connected in series so that power generated by each cell cutting piece can be efficiently collected and transmitted through the module.

Adjacent cell cutting pieces are connected by a connector. The connector is configured to electrically link a front electrode of one cell cutting piece to a first surface of the connector, and to electrically link a back electrode of an adjacent cell cutting piece to a second surface of the connector. In this way, the connector establishes a series connection between neighboring cell cutting pieces while allowing the pieces to be arranged in a compact and stable structure.

The first and second surfaces of the connector include alternating connecting areas and disconnecting areas. More specifically, the first surface includes first connecting areas and first disconnecting areas, while the second surface includes second connecting areas and second disconnecting areas. The connecting areas provide electrical contact with corresponding electrodes of the cell cutting pieces, whereas the disconnecting areas are configured to avoid electrical contact where connection is not required.

In addition, the connector is structured so that projections of the first disconnecting areas overlap with projections of the second connecting areas. This alternating and overlapping arrangement helps distribute stress applied to the connector and the cell cutting pieces. As a result, the module can better accommodate bending, vibration, thermal expansion, and other mechanical forces that may occur during manufacturing, installation, or use.

Through this configuration, the solar cell module achieves enhanced flexibility and improved mechanical reliability. The risk of damage to grid lines, electrodes, or the solar cell cutting pieces themselves is reduced, thereby improving the overall durability and service life of the module. The disclosed manufacturing method enables the cell cutting pieces to be cut, stacked, and connected in series using the connector structure described above, producing a solar cell module suitable for applications requiring both efficient electrical performance and resistance to mechanical breakage.
outputs.L4:
A solar cell module and a method for manufacturing the same are provided. The solar cell module includes a plurality of solar cell pieces formed by cutting solar cells into smaller sections. These cut cell pieces are arranged in a stacked or overlapping configuration and are electrically connected to one another in series. By using smaller cell pieces rather than full-sized cells, the module can more easily bend or conform to an external force, thereby improving flexibility and reducing mechanical stress.

Each solar cell piece includes a front electrode formed on a light-receiving surface and a back electrode formed on an opposite surface. A connector is used to electrically connect adjacent solar cell pieces. The connector has a first surface and a second surface, and includes alternating connecting areas and disconnecting areas. The connecting areas are configured to make electrical contact with the electrodes of the solar cell pieces, while the disconnecting areas prevent unwanted electrical contact. In particular, connecting areas on one surface of the connector may be connected to front electrodes of one or more solar cell pieces, and connecting areas on the opposite surface may be connected to back electrodes of adjacent solar cell pieces. Through this arrangement, the solar cell pieces are connected in series in a reliable and compact manner.

The alternating arrangement of connecting and disconnecting areas allows the connector to establish the desired electrical path between neighboring cell pieces while preventing short circuits. This configuration also enables adjacent cell pieces to be partially overlapped or stacked without requiring complicated wiring structures. As a result, the overall module can maintain high electrical performance while having a simplified interconnection structure.

In the manufacturing method, a plurality of solar cells may first be prepared and then divided into smaller cell pieces by cutting. The cell pieces are arranged so that the front electrode of one cell piece and the back electrode of another cell piece can be connected through the connector. The connector is positioned between or across the overlapping regions of adjacent cell pieces. Conductive bonding material, solder, conductive adhesive, or another suitable electrical connection material may be applied to the connecting areas of the connector. The cell pieces and connector are then bonded together so that the intended series electrical connection is formed. The assembled cell pieces may subsequently be encapsulated between protective layers, such as an encapsulant sheet, a front cover, and a back sheet, to form the completed solar cell module.

Because the module is formed from multiple cut cell pieces and uses a connector designed with selective connection regions, stress generated during bending, handling, installation, or thermal expansion can be distributed more effectively. This reduces the likelihood that grid lines, bus bars, or the solar cell pieces themselves will crack or break. The structure therefore enhances the mechanical durability and reliability of the solar cell module. In addition, the improved flexibility makes the module suitable for applications requiring curved, lightweight, or bendable photovoltaic panels, while maintaining efficient series connection between the solar cell pieces.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in the English language, but it is also one of the most important. It helps us point to something specific, turning a general idea into a clear one. For example, “a book” could mean any book, but “the book” refers to a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

This simple word gives language direction and meaning. It can make something feel unique, important, or already known. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our sky. We say “the best day” to describe a day that stands above the rest. In this way, “the” helps organize our thoughts and connect them to the world around us.

Although it is often overlooked, “the” appears everywhere: in stories, conversations, songs, and speeches. It is a quiet word, but without it, English would feel less precise and less natural. Sometimes, the smallest words carry the greatest weight.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a solar cell module with cut cell pieces connected in series by a connector having alternating connecting and disconnecting areas on opposite surfaces.
counterfactuals.output: A solar cell module includes a plurality of cut cell pieces arranged in a row and electrically connected in series. A connector extends across adjacent cut cell pieces and includes alternating connecting areas and disconnecting areas disposed on opposite surfaces of the connector. A connecting area on one surface of the connector is electrically coupled to an electrode of a first cut cell piece, and a connecting area on the opposite surface is electrically coupled to an electrode of an adjacent second cut cell piece, thereby forming a series connection between the cut cell pieces. The disconnecting areas are positioned to prevent electrical contact with corresponding regions of the cut cell pieces and to reduce short-circuiting between electrodes of different polarities. The alternating arrangement of connecting and disconnecting areas enables reliable interconnection of cut cell pieces while reducing module space loss and improving output characteristics of the solar cell module.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise invention summary describing a flexible shingled solar cell module where front and back electrodes are connected through patterned connector regions.
counterfactuals.output: A flexible shingled solar cell module includes a plurality of thin, overlapping solar cell strips arranged in a shingled configuration on a flexible substrate. Each solar cell strip has a front electrode and a back electrode. Patterned connector regions are formed at selected overlap areas between adjacent strips to electrically couple the front electrode of one strip to the back electrode of a neighboring strip. The connector regions may include conductive adhesive, metal traces, vias, or printed conductive materials arranged in predefined patterns to provide reliable series interconnection while maintaining mechanical flexibility. The patterned regions localize electrical contact, reduce shading and resistive losses, and accommodate bending stresses, enabling a lightweight, conformable photovoltaic module suitable for curved or flexible surfaces.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an English patent abstract for the following invention: solar cell cutting pieces stacked in series, each with front/back electrodes, using a double-sided connector whose non-connection regions overlap opposite-side connection regions to reduce breakage.
counterfactuals.output: A solar cell module includes a plurality of solar cell pieces obtained by cutting solar cells, the solar cell pieces being stacked or arranged in series and each having a front-surface electrode and a back-surface electrode. Adjacent solar cell pieces are electrically connected by a double-sided connector having conductive connection regions on opposite surfaces thereof. A first connection region on one surface of the connector is connected to an electrode of one solar cell piece, and a second connection region on the opposite surface is connected to an electrode of an adjacent solar cell piece, thereby forming a series connection. The connector further includes non-connection regions on each surface. At least one non-connection region on one surface is disposed so as to overlap, in a thickness direction of the connector, a connection region on the opposite surface. This overlapping arrangement disperses mechanical stress generated during bonding, stacking, or module operation, thereby suppressing cracking or breakage of the solar cell pieces and improving reliability of the solar cell module.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a technical disclosure paragraph for a solar cell module and its manufacturing method, emphasizing improved flexibility and prevention of grid line or cell cracking.
counterfactuals.output: A solar cell module and a method of manufacturing the same are disclosed, wherein the module includes a plurality of solar cells electrically interconnected by conductive interconnect members and encapsulated between a front protective member and a rear protective member with an encapsulant layer disposed therebetween. Each solar cell includes grid lines formed on at least one surface thereof, and the interconnect members are arranged and bonded so as to reduce localized mechanical stress applied to the grid lines and the cell substrate during bending or thermal cycling. In one embodiment, a flexible stress-relief layer, patterned adhesive region, or segmented conductive ribbon is provided between the interconnect member and the solar cell to permit relative displacement and distribute strain over a wider area. The manufacturing method includes forming grid lines on the solar cells, positioning the cells with predetermined spacing, electrically connecting adjacent cells using flexible or stress-relieved interconnect members, laminating the connected cells with an encapsulant under controlled temperature and pressure, and curing the encapsulant to form an integrated flexible module. By improving strain distribution and suppressing concentration of stress at the grid-line connection portions, the module exhibits enhanced flexibility and reduced occurrence of grid line breakage, solder joint failure, and cracking of the solar cells.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a patent claim-like abstract about a photovoltaic module made from multiple cut solar cells connected by connectors with alternating first/second connecting and disconnecting areas.
counterfactuals.output: A photovoltaic module comprises a plurality of cut solar cells arranged in a cell string, each cut solar cell including a front-side electrode and a rear-side electrode. Adjacent cut solar cells are electrically interconnected by a plurality of elongate connectors extending across the cut solar cells. Each connector includes, along a longitudinal direction thereof, alternating first connecting areas and second connecting areas configured to be electrically coupled to respective electrodes of adjacent cut solar cells, and disconnecting areas disposed between the first and second connecting areas. The first connecting areas are bonded to electrodes of a first cut solar cell, and the second connecting areas are bonded to electrodes of a second cut solar cell adjacent to the first cut solar cell, such that the connectors provide serial electrical connection between the adjacent cut solar cells. The disconnecting areas are configured to be free of electrical bonding to the cut solar cells, to reduce mechanical stress, accommodate thermal expansion, and improve reliability of the photovoltaic module.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
